correctness.rationale: The claim concerns integers k>=2 and k-1<=d<=2k-3, all finite bipartite G and all induced H (including disconnected and empty under zero conventions). A shortest H-geodesic of length <=d alternates bipartition sides and contains at most ceil((d+1)/2)<=k-1 vertices of either side, yielding a two-color k,d-independent partition. If no k-vertex geodesic hyperedge exists, chi=1 and omega=min(|V(H)|,k-1), so ceil(omega/(k-1))=1 for nonempty H. If one exists, chi=2 and omega>=k. Any 2k-1 vertices have >=k on one bipartition side, which cannot be a geodesic hyperedge, hence omega<=2k-2. Thus ceil(omega/(k-1))=2=chi for every induced subgraph. The exact hypotheses k>=2 and d<=2k-3 are critical; beyond this strip the same proof does not apply. Small finite graph hyperedges independently reconstructed from geodesics; all-graph proof is combinatorial.
